_provenance.claim: DISTRIBUTIONAL ONLY. np.random.choice draws from numpy's global RNG, so no SCX output reproduces its draws. The probabilities here follow torch's precision — log1p and the normalisation in float32, widened once the way numpy widens p — while SCX's kernel accumulates its CDF in f64, so a value sitting exactly on a boundary can fall either way. That remaining difference is a declared divergence. The frozen SCX draws live in sample_golden.json, whose source of truth is Rust (regenerate with the #[ignore]d test).
